- Work only inside this project directory.

brief.title: Invoices
brief.body:
The invoices page of a small-business billing app.

- A table of about 25 invoices: number, customer, issue date, due date, amount and status (draft,
  sent, paid, overdue).
- Filters above the table: a search box that matches invoice number or customer, a status filter
  and a date range for the issue date. Show how many invoices match.
- Amounts are in US dollars and line up so they are easy to compare.
- Each row has a menu with "View", "Download PDF" and "Mark as paid" (only for unpaid invoices).
- When no invoice matches the filters, say so and offer to clear the filters.
- The page must also work on a phone.
brief.markdown:
# Invoices

The invoices page of a small-business billing app.

- A table of about 25 invoices: number, customer, issue date, due date, amount and status (draft,
  sent, paid, overdue).
- Filters above the table: a search box that matches invoice number or customer, a status filter
  and a date range for the issue date. Show how many invoices match.
- Amounts are in US dollars and line up so they are easy to compare.
- Each row has a menu with "View", "Download PDF" and "Mark as paid" (only for unpaid invoices).
- When no invoice matches the filters, say so and offer to clear the filters.
- The page must also work on a phone.

scores.evidence: Spacing is handled by Section, SectionHeader and the design system's components. The page itself adds only a few scale steps: gap-4 in the filter grid, gap-3 between mobile cards and gap-2 inside cards. The filter, count and table groups are separated more widely than the rows within them.

The level-1 SectionHeader title is the focal point, and the description sits in muted text. Row menus use ghost icon-sm buttons, and Clear filters is ghost. The only primary actions are Clear filters in the Empty state and Close in the dialog, with Download PDF and Mark as paid stepped down to outline.

The Amount header and cells use text-end with tabular-nums, and the filter controls share one height on a shared baseline. Table columns and mobile cards start on one edge, and the amount lines up with the status badge row.

The no-match view is an Empty with an icon, an explanation and a Clear filters button. An aria-live count reads '25 invoices' or 'N of 25 invoices match'. Mark as paid gives a toast and updates the badge. The date inputs use min/max to stop a reversed range, but Download PDF only shows a toast and downloads nothing.
There are no custom animations. The only motion comes from the library's Dialog, DropdownMenu, Select and Toaster components, which use the motion tokens.

Every filter has a FieldLabel, and the Select trigger uses aria-labelledby. The form has role=search. Each row trigger is named aria-label='Actions for INV-xxxx', and the Actions column has an sr-only header. Status is shown as a text Badge, and the mobile list has an aria-label.

There are no literal colors or lengths. Styling comes from component variants (Badge muted, info, success and error) and role classes such as text-muted-foreground and text-foreground. The only className additions are layout utilities.

The steps mostly come from the scale (mb-1, mt-1, mt-3, mt-4, mb-6, mt-6), but they are set as margins on individual children. The rhythm also varies: the filter footer mixes mt-4 and pt-3, the menu cell uses px-2 py-2 while other cells use px-4 py-3, and mobile cards pull the menu in with -mt-1 -mr-2.

The text-2xl/3xl semibold h1 leads the page, and the uppercase xs headers in slate-500 step down. Clear filters in the filter footer is a text-style link, so the solid blue button appears only in the empty state and as Mark as paid in the dialog. On mobile, the amount is set in text-lg semibold as each card's focal point.

The Amount header and cells use text-right with tabular-nums, dates are tabular as well, and the filter controls share py-2 heights. On mobile, a dt/dd grid aligns the Issued and Due values, and the amount sits at the end of each card.

The dashed EmptyState explains why no invoices match and offers Clear filters. An invalid date range shows an inline error, linked through aria-invalid and aria-describedby, and the aria-live count shows 'N of 25 invoices match' with a total. Download PDF really builds and downloads a PDF, and each action shows a toast.
There are no animations or transitions, only hover background changes. The menu, dialog and toast appear without motion, so nothing is decorative or loops.

The page uses native label/htmlFor, a select and a dialog with aria-labelledby. The custom menu has role=menu, arrow, Home, End and Escape keys, and returns focus to its trigger. Menu buttons are size-10 with aria-label names, statuses are text badges, and focus-visible rings are present.

Colors are Tailwind palette literals throughout: bg-slate-50, text-slate-900, bg-blue-600, text-blue-700, and a STATUS_STYLES map of emerald, red and blue classes. The design-system components are not used, and the dialog has a one-off w-[calc(100%-2rem)].

brief.title: Notification settings
brief.body:
A settings page where a signed-in user of a team chat app decides which notifications they get.

- Three groups: "Messages" (direct messages, mentions, replies in threads you follow), "Channels"
  (new channels, channel invites) and "Account" (security alerts, product news).
- Each notification has a short description and a switch per delivery channel: email, push and
  in-app.
- Security alerts by email cannot be turned off; say why.
- A "Quiet hours" section with a switch and a start and end time.
- Changes are not saved until the user presses "Save changes". The button is disabled until
  something changes and shows progress while saving (fake it with a one-second delay), and a short
  confirmation appears when the save succeeds. A "Discard" action resets the form.
brief.markdown:
# Notification settings

A settings page where a signed-in user of a team chat app decides which notifications they get.

- Three groups: "Messages" (direct messages, mentions, replies in threads you follow), "Channels"
  (new channels, channel invites) and "Account" (security alerts, product news).
- Each notification has a short description and a switch per delivery channel: email, push and
  in-app.
- Security alerts by email cannot be turned off; say why.
- A "Quiet hours" section with a switch and a start and end time.
- Changes are not saved until the user presses "Save changes". The button is disabled until
  something changes and shows progress while saving (fake it with a one-second delay), and a short
  confirmation appears when the save succeeds. A "Discard" action resets the form.

Only the switch moves (`transition-colors` and `transition-transform`), and only the loader spins, to show progress. Durations and easings are Tailwind defaults rather than `--a63-motion-*` tokens, and nothing handles reduced motion.

The custom switch is a `<button role="switch">` with `aria-checked`, a full aria-label and `aria-describedby` pointing to the lock reason, and it has a visible focus outline. Cards are sections named by `aria-labelledby` their h2, and the save status is carried by text and an icon, not color alone.

brief.title: First project
brief.body:
What a new user of a design feedback tool sees right after signing up, before they have any
projects.

- The page explains in one or two sentences what a project is and why they would create one.
- One primary action, "Create your first project", and a secondary way to "Import from Figma".
- Below it, a short checklist of three getting-started steps (create a project, invite a teammate,
  share a link for feedback), each with a one-line explanation. The first step is the current one;
  the others are not done yet.
- A link to a two-minute video tour.
- Pressing "Create your first project" opens a small dialog that asks for a project name and
  creates it. After that, the page shows the new project in a list and the checklist marks the
  first step done.
